spec_match.rationale: Exercises display-p3-linear as a <rectangular-color-space> per CSS Color 4's interpolation-space section, in both linear-gradient color-interpolation-method syntax and color-mix(), each probed with its own exact CSS.supports expression.

interactive.rationale: Two stop pickers re-render three gradient bars and three color-mix midpoint chips with computed-value readbacks on every input.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The card promises three interpolation spaces plus a color-mix midpoint readout, which the page renders.

edge_cases.rationale: The unsupported space renders an explicit hatched 'no gradient shown' panel — never a lookalike gradient — and the mix row prints 'rejected by this browser'; the srgb/srgb-linear pair keeps the gamma-vs-linear comparison alive on pre-144 browsers.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/5162372125818880 and the interpolation-space spec section.

conformance.rationale: Suite assertions color-mix-in-display-p3-linear and gradient-in-display-p3-linear pin exactly these two syntax contracts; suite verified executing on /conformance/.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 (chrome-devtools-mcp unavailable here): desktop screenshot read — in srgb dips dark through the middle, in srgb-linear stays luminous, display-p3-linear shows the explicit unsupported panel; DOM dump shows the computed srgb-linear mix color(srgb-linear 0.5 0.288752 0.007998); CDP clean console, no overflow at 360.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts interpolation-bars-rendered with the per-space support map and the distinct p3-linear-interpolation-native / -unsupported-fallback branch.

design_system.rationale: Token-based chrome; supported/unsupported badges are text on accent-emerald/accent-amber; gradient stop colours are demo content, not UI chrome.

accessibility.rationale: Gradient bars have role=img with aria-labels naming the space and stops (or the unsupported state), stop pickers are labelled native inputs, the summary is aria-live, and support state is worded, not colour-coded only.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Bars are fluid width and the label lines wrap; CDP-measured no horizontal overflow at 360x740 DPR3; both class screenshots read.

openQuestions.title: Compare in display-p3 vs in display-p3-linear on wide-gamut hardware
openQuestions.detail: On a 144+ browser attached to a P3 display, add an eyeball comparison between in display-p3 and in display-p3-linear interpolation of out-of-sRGB stops — the difference only fully materialises when the display can actually show P3. Needs both a 144 engine and P3 hardware, neither present in this environment (color-gamut: p3 reported false).

guidanceConsulted.query: modern css gradient interpolation color spaces
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Prefer feature-queried modern CSS with graceful degradation for unsupported syntax.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Each bar renders only behind its own CSS.supports check for the exact interpolation-method syntax; unsupported syntax yields an explicit labelled panel rather than a broken or faked rendering.

guidanceConsulted.query: alternative text for purely visual gradient comparison
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Purely visual comparisons need textual equivalents.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Each bar has an aria-label naming space and stops, and the color-mix section prints the numeric computed midpoint per space, giving a non-visual account of the visual difference.

summary: Practical-use concept: display-p3-linear as an interpolation space for gradients and color-mix, probed syntax-by-syntax and rendered only where genuinely supported, with computed midpoints as numeric evidence. On Chromium 141 the two legacy spaces demonstrate the linear-light difference and the new space shows its honest unsupported panel. Verified at both device classes.
